subject: accounting
text: Which statement shows the financial position at a point in time?
explanation: The balance sheet reports assets, liabilities and equity at a single date.
objective: The balance sheet reports assets, liabilities and equity at a single date.

subject: accounting
text: Which account is increased by a debit entry?
explanation: Debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, equity and revenue.
objective: Debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, equity and revenue.

subject: accounting
text: What is a trial balance used to check?
explanation: It verifies the ledger is arithmetically balanced before preparing statements.
objective: It verifies the ledger is arithmetically balanced before preparing statements.

subject: accounting
explanation: Every transaction records equal and opposite entries so the accounting equation stays balanced.
objective: Every transaction records equal and opposite entries so the accounting equation stays balanced.

subject: accounting
text: Why is depreciation added back in the operating cash flow?
explanation: Depreciation lowered net profit without any cash leaving, so it is added back to reconcile to cash.
objective: Depreciation lowered net profit without any cash leaving, so it is added back to reconcile to cash.

subject: accounting
text: What does the current ratio measure?
explanation: Current assets over current liabilities shows whether short-term obligations can be met.
objective: Current assets over current liabilities shows whether short-term obligations can be met.

subject: accounting
text: How does FIFO affect closing inventory during rising prices?
explanation: The oldest (cheapest) purchases are sold first, so the newer costlier stock stays in closing inventory.
objective: The oldest (cheapest) purchases are sold first, so the newer costlier stock stays in closing inventory.

subject: accounting
text: Compute the inventory turnover ratio for a given period, rounded to two decimals.
explanation: Turnover divided by 365 or 365 days gives days-in-inventory; a zero denominator must not divide by zero.
objective: Turnover divided by 365 or 365 days gives days-in-inventory; a zero denominator must not divide by zero.

subject: accounting
text: Explain deferred revenue and when it is recognised.
explanation: Cash received before delivery is a liability, released to revenue as the performance obligation is satisfied.
objective: Cash received before delivery is a liability, released to revenue as the performance obligation is satisfied.

subject: accounting
text: Why can a very high return on equity be a warning sign?
explanation: ROE rises when equity shrinks, so heavy borrowing can inflate the ratio without improved performance.
objective: ROE rises when equity shrinks, so heavy borrowing can inflate the ratio without improved performance.
